9409799c158fa716806104bbd29b5c4cfca7d939.summary: Report by Ireneusz Tarnowski on INC Ransom, a Ransomware-as-a-Service double-extortion group observed since mid-2023 and among the most active operators in 2025–2026. Analysis of an exposed server and a Rust-written sample (agent.exe) describes Active Directory Group Policy and Impacket being used to push a payload that disables Microsoft Defender and UAC, then encrypts files with a .INC extension. The group relies on LOLBins, RMM tools and Cobalt Strike, and the report includes Sigma detection rules. Initial access is not confirmed, and exfiltration is inferred rather than seen.

hedges: The report says it is not possible to determine from the recovered files how initial access was achieved; the listed access vectors are the most likely ones, not confirmed.
Static analysis did not reveal conclusive evidence of command-and-control communication; networking during execution cannot be ruled out.
The exact use of the Windows Service Control Manager functions requires confirmation through dynamic analysis.
Data exfiltration most likely occurred at an earlier stage of the intrusion, since no exfiltration script was found among the recovered files.
The analysis does not cover the earlier stages of the compromise, including the initial intrusion or the infrastructure used to manage the operation.
Limited variation in TTPs may indicate either a small number of affiliates or a more selective affiliate program.
Similarity to LockBit and BlackCat should not be read as evidence of any direct organizational relationship between these groups.
The report assesses that the total number of victims by the end of the year may exceed the 2025 figure, unless operations are disrupted.

948b1c05863cec0266517441f5ad68a8bcf7267a.summary: BleepingComputer reports that the BlackCat/ALPHV ransomware gang appears to be running an exit scam. Its leak site and negotiation servers went offline, affiliates say they were not paid, and the gang offered its source code for $5 million. The gang posted a fake FBI seizure banner, which Europol and the NCA denied being involved in. The gang had earlier been linked to the Change Healthcare attack, and the report says it is unclear whether the group will return under a new name.

94cf359a01b554eb46edd83952e99930d114046c.summary: FireEye's June 2017 threat research blog post says targeted attackers, including FIN8, FIN7, APT19 and APT32, increasingly used command-line obfuscation and application whitelisting bypass techniques in phishing lures and macros during 2017. Examples include PowerShell commands passed via environment variables and standard input, WMI-spawned command processes, and shortcut files hidden in phishing documents. The report links FIN8 to the PUNCHTRACK POS-scraping malware and urges defenders not to rely on a single detection method.

9468ff9d1bc06b4c9f187e4ab55ae485750d6c5b.summary: FireEye FLARE analysis of a leaked CARBANAK source code dump. It confirms the code is CARBANAK and describes antivirus evasions disclosed to vendors (AVG, Trend Micro), public exploits used for privilege elevation, copied Mimikatz code, hardcoded passwords and keys, and network indicators overlapping earlier CARBANAK activity and FIN7. Author identities remain largely unknown; the malware refers to itself as 'bot'. CVE ids in the exploit table are split across lines and are not recorded.
